name: Thessaloniki
title: Thessaloniki Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships
description: Ship thickness measurement in Thessaloniki for bulk carriers, tankers and feeders: hull structure UTM at berth or anchor, and renewal survey gauging.
h1: Thickness Gauging and Hull Inspection for Ships in Thessaloniki
intro: Thessaloniki is the main port of northern Greece and a gateway for cargo moving to and from the Balkans, so the ships here are mostly working cargo rather than lying in a repair yard: bulk carriers loading or discharging grain, minerals, fertiliser and steel, container feeders, and tankers serving the refinery. That shapes the gauging we do. We mobilise a team from India to take readings during cargo stays and at anchor in the Thermaic Gulf, planned around the cargo programme.

highlights.p: Ships at Thessaloniki are usually working cargo, so gauging is built into port calls. Holds are measured as they are emptied, ballast tanks as cargo operations allow, and decks and coamings whenever the hatch covers are open.

Grain, minerals, fertiliser and steel products moving to and from the Balkan hinterland bring mostly Handysize and Supramax bulk carriers and multipurpose ships, many of them older tonnage on regional trades.
Ships waiting for a berth or for orders lie in the Thermaic Gulf off the port. A few days at anchor is a practical window for pre-docking gauging ahead of a yard call in southern Greece or abroad.

port.h: The Port of Thessaloniki and its shipping
p: The Port of Thessaloniki, run by ThPA S.A., sits at the head of the Thermaic Gulf and is the main cargo port of northern Greece. Its piers handle containers, dry bulk, general cargo and project cargo, and its hinterland reaches well beyond Greece into North Macedonia, Serbia, Bulgaria and Kosovo, with rail and road corridors running north from the quays. The ships that call reflect that role: container feeders and regional services linking to the Mediterranean transhipment hubs, Handysize and Supramax bulk carriers, multipurpose and general cargo ships, and product tankers connected with the HELLENiQ ENERGY refinery west of the city.

Most of these ships are on cargo stays rather than in a yard. A bulk carrier discharging grain or loading minerals may be alongside for several days, and the sequence of cargo work sets which holds and tanks are available at any time. That makes Thessaloniki a port for planned, incremental gauging. A technical manager who knows the ship's renewal survey is approaching can use one or two calls here to measure holds, hatch covers, coamings and ballast tanks, building up the data set before the ship goes to dock and reducing both the work and the uncertainty left for the yard.

Inspection demand also follows the age profile of the regional fleets. Many of the bulk carriers and general cargo ships in Balkan, Black Sea and eastern Mediterranean trades are older ships that change hands often, which brings pre-purchase and on-hire condition gauging. Heavy cargoes such as steel products and scrap are hard on hold structure: grabs and magnets dent tank tops and hopper plating, and impact damage on frames and brackets accelerates local wastage. On ships in those trades we measure frames, brackets, tank tops and lower hopper strakes closely, because that is where condition diverges from the last survey record fastest.

facilities.h: Where gauging is done in and around Thessaloniki
p: Inside the port, gauging takes place at the bulk and general cargo piers and at the container terminal, always within ThPA's ISPS and safety rules and coordinated through the ship's agent. Bulk and multipurpose ships are the most practical: holds can be measured as they are cleared, and hatch covers and coamings are reachable whenever covers are open. On container ships the work usually concentrates on ballast tanks, deck structure and piping, including scrubber systems, because terminal stays are shorter and cargo spaces are rarely empty.

Outside the port, tankers serving the refinery berths and ships at anchor in the Thermaic Gulf are reached by launch. Northern Greece has no ship-repair cluster on the scale of Perama or Elefsina, so ships needing major steel renewal usually dock elsewhere. Gauging in Thessaloniki is therefore most valuable as preparation, giving the owner a measured steel estimate before the ship sails for its yard and letting the superintendent compare yard offers on the same set of readings. For anyone arranging ship inspection in northern Greece, that preparatory role is the realistic one, and the scope is best planned with the docking yard's needs in mind.
list: Bulk and general cargo piers — hold, hatch cover, coaming and frame gauging on bulk carriers and multipurpose ships as cargo operations free each hold
Container terminal — ballast tank, deck and scrubber piping checks on feeders and regional container ships during terminal stays
Refinery and fuel terminals west of the city — deck, deck piping and ballast tank gauging on product tankers within terminal permit rules
Thermaic Gulf anchorage — pre-docking, pre-purchase and condition gauging on ships waiting for berths or orders, reached by launch
Project cargo berths — tank top, hold and lashing-area gauging on multipurpose and heavy-lift ships between cargo operations

context.h: Rules and trade context for Thessaloniki
p: As an EU port, Thessaloniki falls under the Paris MoU, with inspections carried out by the Hellenic Coast Guard, and EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime apply to voyages to and from it. The Mediterranean emission control area, in force since 1 May 2025, covers the Aegean, so ships calling here must burn 0.10% sulphur fuel or use a scrubber. On container feeders and bulk carriers fitted with open-loop scrubbers, the wash-water discharge and overboard sections deserve checking, because pitting through to leakage there is a known failure that leads to unplanned repairs and, if found at sea, to an awkward call with the flag.

Thessaloniki's trades also differ from those of southern Greece. The landlocked Balkan states rely on the port, and the Black Sea is a short voyage away through the Turkish Straits, so many ships calling here also work Black Sea and eastern Mediterranean ports with frequent cargo changes. Owners of such ships often have no superintendent attending, so the gauging plan and the report need to be clear enough to act on remotely: readings tied to frame numbers, photographs of the worst areas, and a short summary of what needs attention before the next survey.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Thessaloniki
jobs.p: Here the scope is usually built around a cargo call. The superintendent tells us which holds and tanks will be accessible and when; we plan readings to follow the discharge or loading sequence, and send results area by area so the rest can be scheduled for the next call or the yard. Bulk carrier gauging in Thessaloniki is the most common case.
list: Hold and topside tank gauging on a Supramax discharging grain, measured hold by hold as each is emptied, to build the data set for its third renewal survey.
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a general cargo ship alongside, covering hatch covers, coamings, tank top and ballast tanks before the buyer confirms the purchase.
Scrubber overboard and wash-water piping inspection on a container feeder during a terminal stay, after a leak was reported on a sister ship.
Pre-docking gauging on a product tanker at anchor in the Thermaic Gulf ahead of its intermediate survey, focused on deck plating and ballast tanks.
On-hire gauging on a Handysize bulk carrier delivering into a time charter, giving owner and charterer an agreed record of hold and hatch cover condition.

logistics: The team flies into Thessaloniki Airport Makedonia, usually connecting through Athens or another European hub, and reaches the port by road. Port entry under ISPS is arranged through the ship's agent, who also books launches for ships at anchor in the Thermaic Gulf; we send crew lists, technician certificates and equipment lists in advance. Greece is a Schengen state, so technicians travel on Schengen visas obtained in India. Because cargo calls can be fixed at short notice, it helps to tell us about likely Thessaloniki calls early, so a visa is already in hand when the berth date firms up.

faqs.q: Can you gauge cargo holds while the ship is discharging in Thessaloniki?
faqs.a: Yes, hold by hold. Once a hold is discharged and swept and the stevedores have moved on, we can measure tank top, hopper and side plating and frames safely, with access arranged with the ship. Holds still under cargo are left for a later call or the yard. We agree the sequence with the master and agent so the gauging follows the cargo work rather than delaying it.

faqs.q: There is no large repair yard nearby. Why gauge here rather than in dock?
faqs.a: Because readings taken before the ship reaches the yard let you estimate steel renewal, compare yards and order plate in advance. A ship that arrives in dock with its gauging largely done spends less time waiting while the scope is discovered. Thessaloniki calls, especially longer bulk discharges, are a practical place to do that preparation.

faqs.q: Do you work on ships at anchor in the Thermaic Gulf?
faqs.a: Yes. The agent books a launch, and we board with portable equipment for ballast tanks, holds and deck. Launch transfers depend on sea state, especially in winter, so we leave some slack in the plan for anchorage jobs. Before work starts, the ship has to ventilate, test and certify each tank as safe for entry.

faqs.q: Can the same mobilisation cover ships in Piraeus or Turkish ports?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Thessaloniki is a short flight from Athens, and the Turkish Aegean and Marmara ports are not far. Where the dates line up, we can plan one trip covering several ships, though Turkey needs a separate visa from the Schengen one, so tell us early which countries are involved.
